task.description:
REWORK ITERATION 1 on the ISS-0911 design. REVIEWER's full FAIL verdict (handoffs/WF03-ISS0911-20260930/step-03d-reviewer.json's result.summary -- read it in full) found a defect the design's own §1 missed: InstanceBoardPage.tsx now has TWO effects independently writing startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId -- the pre-existing effect (driven by definitionId/useDefinition(definitionId)) and the new one (driven by the debounced exact-name lookup). On a 'found' transition, the new effect sets both values correctly AND calls setSearchParams(definitionId=...), which changes the definitionId prop on the next render and RE-TRIGGERS the OLD effect -- before useDefinition(newDefinitionId) has any cache entry for a brand-new id. The old effect then runs with activeDefinitionByName still undefined, transiently blanking startDefinitionVersion back to '' while startDefinitionId stays correct via its '?? definitionId' fallback -- the version display and the submit-target id go briefly out of sync again (the exact invariant ISS-0891 established), plus an avoidable duplicate GET /definitions/:id fires.

Redesign the effect interaction so there is a SINGLE write path for startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId, not two effects racing via a shared side channel (the URL search param). Two directions worth considering (choose and justify one, or propose a better one): (a) make the old (definitionId-driven) effect a no-op when the definitionId change originated from the new effect's own setSearchParams call (e.g. a ref-based 'last set by us' guard comparing the incoming definitionId against what the new effect just wrote); (b) fold both effects into one, with a single reducer-shaped state update that only ever has one effect writing these two fields, and have the definitionId-driven path and the name-lookup-driven path both funnel into that one writer rather than each owning independent effects. Update lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md with the corrected design. Update the acceptance criteria/section stating the invariant explicitly: 'the version display and submitted definitionId are always the same value at the same time, with no intermediate render showing one updated and not the other, even when a URL search-param write triggered by this fix's own new effect re-renders the component.'
acceptance_criteria: the fix calls definitionsApi.getActive(name) (or an equivalent exact-match backend lookup) keyed on the dialog's own typed value, not the page-level filtered list
a race-guard against out-of-order async responses (rapid typing) is explicitly designed, not left implicit
the version field's loading/not-found/found states are all specified

NEW (this rework): a single write path for startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId is designed, with no possibility of the new effect's own setSearchParams call re-triggering a second, independent effect that transiently desyncs the two values

result.summary: Redesigned §5.2 of lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md to fold the two independently-writing effects (definitionId/useDefinition(definitionId)-driven, and versionLookupState-driven) into ONE effect with a single write path for startDefinitionVersion/startDefinitionId, per rework option (b) (chosen over (a) because a skip-guard bolted onto the old effect alone still leaves two effects whose relative scheduling order is not part of either's contract -- folding into one effect makes precedence between the two data sources an explicit, single, ordered piece of logic that cannot depend on effect-scheduling order). Design: a new ref, lookupWroteDefinitionId, records the id the effect's own 'found' branch most recently wrote/pushed via setSearchParams. The merged effect's priority order per run: (1) versionLookupState.kind === 'found' -- write both fields from the lookup result (authoritative), record lookupWroteDefinitionId.current, then setSearchParams; (2) 'not_found'/'error' -- clear both fields and clear the ref; (3) 'idle'/'loading' -- fall through to the definitionId-driven source ONLY if definitionId !== lookupWroteDefinitionId.current (i.e. this render's definitionId change was NOT self-caused by step 1's own setSearchParams); if it IS self-caused, do nothing, leaving the values step 1 already wrote untouched -- this guard is what eliminates the bug, since the old effect's blanking write (from stale-uncached activeDefinitionByName) simply never runs for a self-caused definitionId change. Added an explicit top-of-doc 'Rework 1' section stating the invariant verbatim as directed by the task, retracted §1's now-false claim that the old effect was an 'already-correct, untouched' data path, and added a new row to the §8 AC-to-design-element map for this rework's AC4. No implementation code was written -- only type/ref signatures and control-flow prose, consistent with the design-only mandate.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for a fresh full pass
